headline: Copper strength lifts sales; split skews per-share metrics
summary_short: Mueller Industries' Q2 FY2026 net sales rose 25.5% y/y to $1,428M on higher copper prices and volume growth, while net income rose 1.5% y/y to $249.7M; diluted EPS of $1.13 (+1.8% y/y) reflects a two-for-one stock split that also doubled the diluted share count q/q.
summary_long: Net sales rose 25.5% y/y (19.7% q/q) to $1,428M on unit-volume growth across all three segments plus price increases tied to a 30.6% y/y rise in COMEX copper. Gross profit rose 12.0% y/y to $395M. Operating income rose 1.9% y/y to $310.0M; management notes the y/y comparison is muted by a $36.3M insurance gain booked in Q2 2025 — excluding that one-off, operating income rose 15.7% y/y. Net income rose 1.5% y/y to $249.7M; diluted EPS of $1.13 is up 1.8% y/y but down sharply q/q only because Q1's stored share count predates the June 30, 2026 stock split. Cash and short-term investments held near $1.42B after $138.3M was spent acquiring Bison Metals Technologies. No numeric forward guidance was given.

drivers.explanation: Unit volume growth in all three segments plus copper-linked price increases drove sales and earnings higher; the company also closed two metals acquisitions in the quarter (Bison Metals Technologies, Chicago Extruded Metals).
Unit volume growth in each of the three reporting segments, combined with price increases tied to a 30.6% y/y rise in COMEX copper ($6.16/lb average), drove the net sales increase.
The y/y comparison is held down by a $36.3M insurance gain ($28.1M net of tax) recognized in Q2 2025; excluding that prior-year one-off, the company reports a 15.7% y/y increase in operating income.

The apparent q/q EPS/share-count swing is a stock-split artifact, not an operating change: Q1 2026's stored diluted share count (110.9M) predates the June 30, 2026 two-for-one split and is not split-adjusted, while Q2's (221.2M) is, roughly doubling shares and halving per-share figures q/q.
Net cash from operations of $212.3M more than covered $138.3M spent acquiring Bison Metals Technologies, leaving cash and short-term investments near $1.42B with a 4.8:1 current ratio.
